name: Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee

summary.text: The House of Commons Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Committee, chaired during 2017-19 by Damian Collins MP, conducted the Disinformation and 'fake news' inquiry, taking evidence from 73 oral witnesses including Christopher Wylie, Brittany Kaiser and Alexander Nix. It published an interim report (HC 363) on 29 July 2018 and a final report (HC 1791) on 18 February 2019 covering social media platforms' liabilities and data misuse in the Facebook, Cambridge Analytica and AggregateIQ matters. The Information Commissioner's final account of her investigation was a letter to the committee's later chair, Julian Knight MP, dated 2 October 2020.

facts.claim: The committee published its interim report, Disinformation and 'fake news' (HC 363), in July 2018; it warned of a democratic crisis tied to the manipulation of personal data, recommended agreed definitions of misinformation and disinformation, said Facebook had hampered the inquiry, and stated that Nix misled the committee regarding GSR.

facts.claim: The committee's final report (HC 1791) was published on 18 February 2019 after an inquiry with 170 written submissions and 73 oral witnesses; it covered the definition, role and legal liabilities of social media platforms and data misuse and targeting in the Facebook, Cambridge Analytica and AggregateIQ matters.

facts.claim: The final report's chapter on SCL influence in foreign elections recorded that Cambridge Analytica pitched to Lukoil while SCL Group was delivering counter-Russian propaganda training for NATO, and repeated the recommendation that the National Crime Agency investigate the connections between SCL Elections Ltd and Emerdata Ltd.
facts.quote: the National Crime Agency should investigate the connections between the company SCL Elections Ltd and Emerdata Ltd

sources.title: Disinformation and 'fake news': Final Report, chapter 7: SCL influence in foreign elections

facts.claim: The committee took oral evidence from Christopher Wylie on 27 March 2018, Brittany Kaiser on 17 April 2018 and Alexander Nix on 6 June 2018, among 61 witnesses heard by the time of the interim report; Dominic Cummings declined to appear and the committee reported his conduct to the House.
facts.quote: Whistleblower Christopher Wylie and Cambridge Analytica chief executive Alexander Nix were among the 61 witnesses that gave evidence.
